subject: ACME POC evaluation - next steps & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: ACME POC evaluation - next steps & success criteria

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC.

Key pain and goals you shared:
- Improve intent classification accuracy for customer support routing (current pipeline has ~78% accuracy).
- Reduce end-to-end classification latency to meet real-time routing SLAs.
- Keep data in your VPC; no customer PII should leave your environment.

Proposed POC scope (high level):
- Offline evaluation on your labeled holdout set + a 2-week online shadow run on a representative traffic slice.
- Success criteria (initial ask) - please confirm or edit:
  1) Intent classification F1 >= 0.85 on labeled test set;
  2) P95 inference latency < 300ms at target throughput (see below);
  3) No PII exfiltration; integration with your KMS for key management.

Tentative timelines and ownership:
- Kickoff & data handoff: week of 2027-05-25 (owner: Sara Patel at ACME)
- Data ingestion & offline eval prep: 2027-05-26 to 2027-05-28 (owner: Marissa/Dylan)
- Offline eval + rubric grading: 2027-06-01 to 2027-06-07
- Shadow run (online): 2027-06-08 to 2027-06-21
- Decision and next steps: target week of 2027-06-24

We attached a first-draft eval plan (acme_poc_eval_plan_v1.pdf) with proposed test sets, a sample rubric, and required integration checklist. Can you confirm the success criteria above, who will own the data handoff, and whether the tentative timelines work for you? If so, we'll lock dates and get the technical kickoff on the calendar.

Thanks - looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_poc_eval_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME POC evaluation - next steps & success criteria

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. That matches how we saw the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

Success criteria (we'd like to lock these down):
1) Intent classification F1 >= 0.86 on our labeled validation set (we can provide labels).
2) P95 inference latency < 250ms for a steady-state 500 qps load (burst to 1k qps is okay if handled gracefully).
3) False positives on the 'escalate to human' intent must be under 2% (that one's business-critical).

Ownership & data:
- Sara (cc'd) will own the data handoff and provide a sanitized sample by 2027-05-20.
- We can provide a sample payload file and a small labeled set - attaching now.

Timelines: the proposed dates look fine; the only ask is that the shadow run include both production traffic sampling and a small controlled replay so we can compare behavior.

We also have a short security questionnaire (SOC 2 + data residency questions). We'll send that separately; happy to get an NDA in place if that helps speed things.

Best,
John
Principal Product Manager, ACME Corp

Attachment: acme_sample_payloads.csv (CSV, 200 rows)

Subject: Re: ACME POC evaluation - next steps & success criteria

John/Sara - appreciate the quick confirmation and the sample file. Sara - thanks in advance for owning the data handoff.

A couple of notes and a proposed evaluation approach to make sure we're aligned on methodology:

Proposed hybrid evaluation approach
- Offline eval (graded): run model(s) on your labeled holdout and on the provided sample payloads. Use automated metrics + a small human-annotated subset for edge cases.
- Online shadow (2 weeks): mirror a percentage of live traffic to Redwood in shadow mode (no change to production routing) and run controlled replay for the same time window so we can compare outputs side-by-side.

Suggested grading rubric (we can iterate):
- Automated metrics (70% weight): F1, precision/recall on labeled set; latency percentiles; throughput.
- Human review (20% weight): sample of 500 shadowed requests, graded for intent correctness and business impact severity.
- Business gating (10% weight): escalation rate, false-positive cost estimate, and operational readiness checklist (infra, KMS, logging).

Milestones (updated)
- 2027-05-20: Sara provides sanitized sample + labeled subset
- 2027-05-25: Technical kickoff
- 2027-05-26 to 2027-05-31: Data ingestion & offline eval prep
- 2027-06-01 to 2027-06-07: Offline eval + rubric scoring
- 2027-06-08 to 2027-06-21: Shadow run + replay comparison
- 2027-06-24: Final review and decision

Next steps for us:
1) I'll incorporate John's latency/false positive targets into the plan and send v1.1 of the eval plan by EOD today.
2) Dylan and I will schedule the technical kickoff once Sara confirms data availability.

If that all looks good I'll send a short mutual action plan (dates/owners) and proposed calendar invites.

Thanks -
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_poc_eval_plan_v1.1.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME POC evaluation - next steps & success criteria

Marissa - quick internal note: I agree with the hybrid approach and the proposed rubric weights. A couple of implementation notes from the infra side:
- We should run automated latency benchmarks under a replayed 500 qps load to validate the P95 target before shadowing. I can spin up the harness and a small dedicated pool for the test.
- For the human review sample, recommend we stratify sampling by low-confidence predictions and high business-impact intents to get better signal.
- Shadowing at 500 qps for two weeks is fine if we enable prefix/KV caching and request sampling (we can start at 10% traffic and ramp).

I'll prepare the eval harness and a runbook for the kickoff.

--Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
